stages.heading: Stardate 2227.00X
commentary: Welcome to yet another AI Solitaire battle, on Experienced difficulty. On the Astrometrics Lab step, a 10 was rolled (none). We randomly choose the Terran faction. On the SP step, a 3 was rolled (400 SP).

For our fleet, we rolled a 4. We field 1 Battlecruiser-X, 1 regular Battlecruiser, and 2 Destroyers. As this is our fleet, we can place them anywhere within our deployment zone; we need only to ensure they share the same direction.

Ticlanat rolls a 7 for its fleet. This gives them 2 Light Cruisers + 4 Destroyers. The leftover 50 SP gives them an extra Destroyer. On the distance step, a 6 was rolled (row farthest from our deployment zone). On the side step, a 5 was rolled (right-hand side). On the formation step, a 3 was rolled (by type).

Luckily, we have built a unique Shuffler just for dealing AI ships, useful whenever they do not roll a balanced formation, and they have more than one type of ship. We use it to draw their first ship; somewhat surprisingly a Light Cruiser. Since the only types they have left are Destroyers, we simply deal the rest of the fleet accordingly.

stages.heading: Stardate 2227.01A
commentary: As usual, the opening impulses are simple; ships are simply too far away to fire weapon groups.

stages.heading: Stardate 2227.01B
commentary: This time, we have the <q>quality</q> advantage. Maybe this is our ticket to winning at a disadvantage.

stages.heading: Stardate 2227.01C
commentary: ... especially since they have relatively few Cobalt Cannons this time around. (1 such weapon per Light Cruiser, for a total of 2.)

stages.heading: Stardate 2227.01D
commentary: At least it is fortunate that we have no battleships to take down... this time.

stages.heading: Stardate 2227.01F
commentary: As usual, we skip impulse Es (and any other empty impulses) as appropriate.

stages.heading: Stardate 2227.01X
commentary: We have made it to the first power phase. Since our Anti-Matter Torpedoes are somewhat inaccurate, we decide the best course of action is to do no change to our power curves.
All of our ships are in front of AI ships; so they neither assign priority targets, nor make changes to their power curves.

stages.heading: Stardate 2227.02A
commentary: The AI moves as usual.

stages.heading: Stardate 2227.02B
commentary: This time, we get to enact some <q>first blood</q>. We will start with our Battlecruiser-X, against Destroyer H7. Our first Anti-Matter Torpedoes rolled 1,6/2,3 (2 hits ≥3), dealing 1 non-critical hull damage against their victim. We will save our Phaser for now.
Next up are our own Destroyers. In reading order, we rolled 2/5 (1 hit ≥3). We have now done enough damage to necessitate they perform a critical roll. 4+5 = 9 (Random Weapon Group Destroyed)

We were unsuccessful against Destroyer H7, but not all hope is lost. We use our last Battlecruiser, and use its Anti-Matter Torpedoes against Destroyer H10. 4,6 were rolled (2 hits ≥3), dealing another 1 non-critical hull damage.

stages.heading: Stardate 2227.02C (AI Impulse)
commentary: The AI moves once more, and this is its first practical chance to shoot. They start with Destroyers G6 and G7, rolling 2/2,5 in the process (1 extra dmg ≥5) against Destroyer E6, depleting our shields exactly.
Destroyer G5 then shoots against Destroyer E6, having rolled 1,3 (0 extra dmg).
Destroyer G9 and Light Cruiser G10 work together against Battlecruiser E8. The Lasers rolled 2,2 (0 extra dmg ≥5), while the Cobalt Cannon rolls a 3 (3 dmg).
Lastly, Destroyer G8 uses its Lasers against Destroyer E7. 3,3 were rolled (0 extra dmg).

stages.heading: Stardate 2227.02C (Player Impulse)
commentary: During our segment of the impulse, we start charging our Anti-Matter Torpedoes. We also fire our Battlecruiser-X's sole Phaser against Destroyer G6, which is almost dead. Even a 1 would finish it off without fail, so we proceed accordingly.

Battlecruiser E8 then uses its 2 Phasers against Destroyer G9. The first roll was a 6 (2 dmg), necessitating a roll of 4+5 for critical damage (Random Weapon Group Destroyed). Since this Destroyer was also knocked down to 1 hull point, even a 1 would finish it off also.

stages.heading: Stardate 2227.02D (AI Impulse)
commentary: The AI repositions its Light Cruisers so that it is better able to use its remaining weapons. Its last Cobalt Cannon rolls a 3 (only 3 dmg), and the Lasers rolled 3,5 (1 extra dmg ≥5). Our Battlecruiser sustains 1 non-critical hull damage.

stages.heading: Stardate 2227.02D (Player Impulse)
commentary: During our segment of the impulse, we order our bigger ships to side slip (using the power that was just generated), and our smaller ships to turn.

stages.heading: Stardate 2227.02F
commentary: Since synergy opportunities were not available in earlier impulses concerning afterburner use, Ticlanat uses none of those <q>consumables</q> at all. Instead, they use the brakes on one of their Light Cruisers to keep it at 2 hexes away from the nearest ship (at the time of their segment).

The other Light Cruiser finally gets a chance to move, but its Lasers are limited to our Battlecruiser's right-hand shields. 4,6 were rolled (1 extra dmg ≥5), cutting our shield quadrant's strength in half. (Attempts to damage our front were extremely unsafe because it would have caused their Light Cruisers to collide!)

stages.heading: Stardate 2227.02X
commentary: We have taken a small lead with these recent kills. Since we recently unleashed all of our weapon groups, and are in the middle of a brawl; we will go on ahead and slow down all of our ships, adjusting our power curves accordingly.
None of our ships are inside the front arcs of the AI ships, so they are all potential priority targets. Comparing the Estimated Fleet Values, we have a slight advantage here too (8 : 7).

Starting at our regular Battlecruiser, a 2 was rolled. This fails even before applying a -2 penalty (≥4 required to assign). Thus, no Priority Targets are assigned. Using the above criteria, all of the AI ships also slow down.

stages.heading: Stardate 2227.03A
commentary: Just because the pace has slowed down does not mean weapons can not be fired. AI Lasers recharge quickly, allowing them to be used again.

We start with their Light Cruisers, since their Lasers could damage our battlecruiser's hull. These Lasers rolled 6,5,5 (6 dmg total) before we reach the critical step. 2+4 = 6 was rolled this way, causing our ship to sustain Manuevering Thruster Damage +1. The last Laser then rolls a 3, not quite enough to finish this battlecruiser off.

Their right-most Destroyers each have a single valid target this impulse. Since it is difficult to optimize their usage further, they will go on ahead and use them anyway. Destroyer E7 rolls 1,4 against Destroyer G6 (2 dmg), while Destroyer E6 rolls 2,3 against the Battlecruiser-X (2 dmg).
<hr />

During our segment of the impulse, we use compatible Phasers (able to shoot off the right side). Battlecruiser-X rolls a 4 against Destroyer E6 (2 dmg). Battlecruiser rolls a 6 against Light Cruiser G9 (also 2 dmg).

stages.heading: Stardate 2227.03B
commentary: While the AI turns their ships around our fleet, they are able to use the last Lasers that were recently recharged. Destroyer E4 rolls 5,6 (2 extra dmg ≥5) against the rear of our battlecruiser-x.
We use our natural power to accelerate turning processes, or to further charge weapons. (In that order.)

stages.heading: Stardate 2227.03C
commentary: Since this is our impulse to move, we do so by turning all of our ships. Since our ships are aligned, it is most practical that we stack turn radius markers on the ships themselves, instead of in front of them.

stages.heading: Stardate 2227.03D
commentary: Granted, we got a few options with our turn radius; accelerate them with power, or (in these cases) prepare side slips.

stages.heading: Stardate 2227.03F
commentary: We are nearing another power phase. Because we turned recently, we messed with the center hex row that their light cruisers were using to determine where to go.
Our Battlecruiser is now able to use its other Phaser against the nearest light cruiser, now that it is in our front. We rolled a 6, dealing 2 damage to the rear shields.

stages.heading: Stardate 2227.03X
commentary: We reach another power phase, where our regular Battlecruiser is down to its last hull point. It is not quite dead though. We slow it down further, to work around its severe hull damage. We also speed our Destroyers back up, now that their Anti-Matter Torpedoes are fully reloaded. Our power curves are adjusted accordingly.
As usual, none of our ships are in front of AI ships. Already this forces them to remain slow (0-3-0). On the PPT step, a 3 was rolled (failure <6), so no priority targets are assigned still.

stages.heading: Stardate 2227.04A
commentary: We have made it to a new round. The AI takes advantage of where its Light Cruisers are positioned, and uses their afterburners to gain a move this impulse.

The ship closest to our battlecruiser can then use its Lasers to finish our ship off, but there is still a small amount of volatility. On the first laser, a 2 was rolled. Since this was not enough to finish our ship off, it then has to use its other laser to do the job. The resulting explosion has damaged Destroyer F9.
One of their Destroyers then shoots against our battlecruiser-x. Their Lasers rolled 3,6, depleting our rear shields exactly; before we reinforce it again.

stages.heading: Stardate 2227.04B
commentary: Here is where things get tricky, but only a little. Most AI ships have an obvious move, but the two Destroyers able to reach G5 risk a collision, necessitating one go around to avoid this issue. Another Destroyer is able to use its Lasers against our battlecruiser-x. 3,6 were rolled again, dealing 2 non-critical hull damage.
<hr />

During our segment, we use both of our Destroyer Anti-Matter Torpedoes. Against Light Cruiser C10's side, we rolled a 1 (miss). Against Light Cruiser D10's front, we rolled a 2 (hit). An opportunity also presents itself where we can use our sole remaining Phaser against Destroyer G6. We rolled a 2, barely dealing 2 damage.

stages.heading: Stardate 2227.04C
commentary: Since our Destroyers moved last impulse, their other light cruiser is able to shoot while remaining stationary. A 5 was rolled (2 dmg), necessitating that a critical roll of 3+6 is made (Random Weapon Group Destroyed). Since that roll did not result in destruction, the other laser was then used to clean it up.
<hr />

During our segment, we move our Battlecruiser-X, and use the Anti-Matter Torpedoes that just reloaded against the front of Light Cruiser D10. A 6, causing 3 hull damage and also a critical roll. A 6+4 (10), an additional 1 damage and causes FTL Offline. Since that was not quite enough, we rolled a 3... which also barely hits. We finish a ship off ourselves! Despite having lost 2 ships, we also negate one of their cobalt cannons!

stages.heading: Stardate 2227.04D
commentary: At this point, nearly all available weapons are exhausted once more.

stages.heading: Stardate 2227.04F
commentary: The AI finally gets to use the last of its Lasers against our battlecruiser-x. 1,3 were rolled, dealing just 2 damage.

stages.heading: Stardate 2227.04X
commentary: Once again, we are no longer ahead of the opposing fleet in terms of SP, thanks to the difficulty setting giving them an extra destroyer. Our Battlecruiser-X is also screwed, since 3 destroyers are chasing its rear. Thus, it matters not how we change its power curve. As for our Destroyer, it stands no chance against an opposition this strong. Since it just finished spooling, we will order it to punch its retreat controls now.

The AI has only our other ship now. Since it happens to be infront of almost all of their ships, they can all safely speed back up except for the destroyer closest to our battlecruiser-x. Not only is our ship technically not in front, any attempt to move towards our ship would render it unable to fire, so it instead stays at 0-3-0.

stages.heading: Stardate 2227.05A
commentary: Our Battlecruiser-X is only able to withstand 3 damage from behind, and they happen to have 6 Lasers available. Even if they were all 1s, and that we rolled a 7 on the critical table, our last ship would still explode.

But, our Battlecruiser-X gets to do one last hurrah before we end this battle for good. 2 of their destroyers happen to be adjacent to our last ship as it was exploding. While one of them simply has their front shields drained, the other ship is already exposed on the quadrant adjacent to us... and just happens to take the exact subsequent hull damage to explode as well. No subsequent chains occur at this point, since AI Destroyers have a natural explosion damage of 0.

stages.heading: Stardate 2227.05B (Game Over)
commentary: While a loss is still a loss, Ticlanat was so close to securing a tactical victory against us. But, the last hurrah proved effective enough to significantly dent their score advantage over us (72% >> 38%). And retreating our last Destroyer was a wise move, as it meant denying them the last 55 SP (potentially allowing a 60% advantage) that would have otherwise kept them out of marginal victory.
